strings.page.title: Game Trees: Minimax and Alpha-Beta Pruning
strings.hero.title: Game Trees: Minimax and Alpha-Beta Pruning
strings.hero.intro: Back terminal utilities up through alternating MAX and MIN turns. Then switch on alpha-beta pruning to see which subtrees can be skipped without changing the exact root decision.
strings.hero.boundary: Model boundary: finite deterministic two-player zero-sum perfect-information trees. Pruned nodes remain visible as part of the problem definition but are labeled not evaluated by the algorithm.
strings.trace.not_started.title: Trace not started
strings.trace.not_started.body: The tree and terminal utilities are visible, but no search event has been revealed.
strings.panel.edit_note: Terminal utilities are the game's given data. Editing one recomputes the trace; it does not mutate the tree topology.
strings.panel.maxmin: MAX keeps the largest returned child value. MIN keeps the smallest. In Alpha-Beta mode, a cutoff is safe once alpha >= beta; skipped nodes are not evaluated.
strings.panel.order: Move ordering can change how much work alpha-beta does. It cannot change the exact minimax value of this fixed tree.
strings.challenge.title: Guided Challenge
strings.challenge.intro: Predict first, lock the prediction, then reveal the deterministic mechanism.
strings.challenge.label: Challenge
strings.challenge.root.label: 1. Predict the root choice
strings.challenge.min.label: 2. Back up a MIN node
strings.challenge.prune.label: 3. Will the branch prune?
strings.challenge.order.label: 4. Which move order does less work?
strings.challenge.greedy.label: 5. Greedy versus minimax
strings.challenge.root.prompt: On the Simple backup tree, which root child will MAX select, and what value reaches the root?
strings.challenge.min.prompt: In Simple backup, node A is a MIN node with terminal children 3 and 5. What value does A return?
strings.challenge.prune.prompt: In First safe prune with Alpha-Beta, will B's remaining child B2 be evaluated after B1 returns 4?
strings.challenge.order.prompt: The Good ordering and Poor ordering scenarios contain the same utilities. Which one makes Alpha-Beta evaluate fewer leaves?
strings.challenge.greedy.prompt: In Greedy trap, branch A contains a visible utility 9. Does minimax select A or B?

strings.challenge.root.actual: MAX selects B; the root value is 4. MIN returns 3 from A and 4 from B, so MAX chooses 4.
strings.challenge.min.actual: A returns 3. MIN keeps the smaller child value.
strings.challenge.prune.actual: Yes. After B1 returns 4, alpha=5 and beta=4, so alpha >= beta. B2 is present in the tree but is not evaluated.
strings.challenge.order.actual: Good ordering evaluates 4 leaves; poor ordering evaluates 6. Both return value 8.
strings.challenge.greedy.actual: Minimax selects B. MIN can force A down to -4, while B guarantees 2; the visible 9 does not determine the root choice.
